dimension_literal_resolution.method: scan info_type/info varlen + parallel id.bin; output: it1_id (int32)
scan info_type/info varlen + parallel id.bin; output: it2_id (int32)

prefilters.notes: Built once by scanning name/gender.bin == 'm'. Probed by person_id from cast_info.

join_order.probe: movie_info_idx via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Drive title id loop. For each tid, probe movie_info_idx__movie_id offsets. If range empty, skip tid (most selective fact filter).
Within CSR range, keep rows where info_type_id == it2_id. Capture candidate mi_idx row positions for projection.

join_order.probe: movie_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Only enter if step 2 produced >=1 mi_idx row for this tid.
Check info_type_id first (int32 cheap), then varlen mi.info via unordered_set<string_view> of 6 literals.

join_order.probe: cast_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Only enter if step 4 produced >=1 mi row for this tid.

join_order.probe: ci.note IN ('(writer)','(head writer)','(written by)','(story)','(story editor)') AND name_gender_m_bitmap[ci.person_id resolved via name__id__pos]
join_order.notes: Note filter via unordered_set<string_view> (5 literals). For surviving rows, look up n.id via name__id__pos[ci.person_id] -> row, then bitmap[row]. Equivalently: since name_gender_m is a per-row bitmap indexed by name row position, and ci.person_id is a name id, use pos[id] -> bitmap[pos].
For tid surviving all probes, update running MIN of mi.info (over qualifying mi rows), mi_idx.info (over qualifying mi_idx rows), and t.title (read once for tid).

data_structures.ci_note_set: unordered_set<string> of 5 literals (lookup via string_view slice)
data_structures.mi_info_set: unordered_set<string> of 6 literals (lookup via string_view slice)
data_structures.aggregation: thread-local running MIN strings; final reduce across threads

parallelism.morsel: title id range (e.g., 16K ids per task)
parallelism.notes: Each thread maintains local MIN(mi.info), MIN(mi_idx.info), MIN(t.title). Final pass reduces 12 candidates.

indexes.purpose: person_id -> name row position for gender bitmap probe
not needed (drive on id directly = row position when contiguous; use id.bin to confirm row=tid mapping if needed)

execution_notes: MIN over varlen requires lexicographic compare; no early exit.
Drive on title to leverage 3 primary CSRs on movie_id simultaneously — all three facts are physically sorted by movie_id, so per-tid probes are contiguous sequential reads (ideal on HDD).
Order of probes (mi_idx -> mi -> ci) is by ascending size: 1.38M < 14.8M < 36.2M rows; skip tid as soon as any probe yields zero qualifying rows.
Apply cheap int32 filters (info_type_id) BEFORE varlen filters (info text) within each CSR range.
ci.note filter is selective (~5%); apply before name gender semijoin to minimize pos/bitmap lookups.
For MIN(t.title): only read title.title for tid that survives all three fact probes (rare).
For MIN(mi.info) and MIN(mi_idx.info): only read varlen for rows that pass all filters for the surviving tid (multiple rows possible per tid; update running min each).

Title row position == tid - 1 if title is dense+sorted; use title__id__pos to be safe, but for sequential drive over tid 1..2528312 we can read title.title.offsets[tid] directly if id maps 1:1 to row.
